keyframe_review.note: 3.20 M km2 for 1836-1839: the union of Cliopatria's Bolivia row (1.81 M km2) and the Republic of Peru's 1835 shape (11,785 of its 11,824 cells; 39 border cells more), the three founding states 'North Peru, South Peru, and Bolivia': every Peruvian department, all Bolivia with Tarija, and the Acre, the Paraguayan Chaco and the Atacama coast that Cliopatria's Bolivia row includes (no page opened describes those). The page gives no area and no boundary description, so no infobox comparison is possible; the page confirms Tarija stayed in Bolivia and that the Confederation was the union of Peru and Bolivia. The shape runs through 1839 although Peru returns in January 1839 (ledger loss, 1839-01) and Bolivia leaves only on 26 October 1839 (ledger loss, 1839-10).

region.text: North Peru and South Peru, the core of the Confederation, with its seat on the Peruvian coast

ledger.note: 1836: Santa Cruz founds the Peru-Bolivian Confederation. 'Santa Cruz decreed the establishment of the Peru-Bolivian Confederation, by decree given in Lima on 28 October 1836'; the Congress of Tacna met on 18 April 1837 and the infobox dates the Pact of Tacna to 1 May 1837.

region.text: the Bolivian Republic, one of the three founding states

ledger.note: 1836: Bolivia joins the Confederation the same day. The Tapacarí Congress had authorised Santa Cruz on 21 June 1836 to complete the confederation project; the decree covers 'North Peru, South Peru, and Bolivia'.

region.text: the city of Arequipa, occupied by the Chilean army landed at Islay

ledger.note: 1837: Chile lands at Islay and occupies Arequipa. 'The Chilean army landed at Islay in southern Peru in October, 1837, occupying the city of Arequipa.' Recorded from the owner's side with the roles reversed: Chile is the occupier (the republic-of-chile dossier should hold the same event).

region.text: Arequipa and the Confederate territory Chile had occupied

ledger.note: 1837: the Treaty of Paucarpata, 17 November 1837, in which Chile agreed to 'withdraw its troops from Confederate territory'; the page gives no date for the departure itself, and Chile repudiated the treaty.

region.text: the 'disputed territories in northern Argentina' that Bolivia occupied in 1838; the War page says Argentina 'lost some territories north of Jujuy'

ledger.note: 1838: the Confederation holds Argentine border land. Page (Confederation): 'Bolivia occupied disputed territories in northern Argentina in 1838'. The page gives no places or month; Jujuy is the researcher's reading of 'north of Jujuy' (Salta, which neither page names, was dropped by the reviewer), and the War of the Confederation page says only that the Argentine Confederation 'lost some territories north of Jujuy'.

region.text: Lima, occupied by the Chilean force

ledger.note: 1838: Chile takes Lima. 'The Chilean force occupied Lima at the end of October, 1838 but abandoned it on November 3'; Lima was occupied again in April 1839, after the Confederation had fallen. Roles reversed as for Arequipa.

region.text: Lima, abandoned by the Chilean force

ledger.note: 1838: the Chileans leave Lima on 3 November 1838 ('abandoned it on November 3').

region.text: the Argentine territories the Confederation had occupied

ledger.note: 1839: the occupied Argentine land is returned. The War page infobox says only that 'the Argentine territories occupied during the war are returned' under a peace agreement between Bolivia and the Argentine Confederation; the page gives no date, so 1839 (the war's end) bridges the silence.

region.text: North and South Peru, merged back into a single Peru

ledger.note: 1839: Yungay breaks the Confederation in Peru. Santa Cruz's army was 'crushed' on 20 January 1839 and he fled to Ecuador; on 25 August 1839 General Gamarra 'officially declared the dissolution of the Confederation and of the North and South-Peruvian Republics', and the two Peruvian states were merged back into one. The page dates the defeat; leaving Peru in January is the researcher's reading, matching the republic-of-peru dossier.

1839: Bolivia leaves the dissolved Confederation. 'Velasco later declared it dissolved on 26 October 1839' (Gamarra's declaration of 25 August is the infobox end date); Bolivia re-emerged as the 'New Bolivian State' and Tarija 'ultimately remained in Bolivia'.

region.text: the Confederation's last shape: Peru and Bolivia

ledger.note: 1839: the Confederation is dissolved. Infobox 'Dissolution declared: 25 August 1839'; Velasco declared it dissolved in Bolivia on 26 October 1839 and Antonio Huachaca's loyalists were beaten in November 1839. The land goes back to Peru (merged into one) and to Bolivia.

wars.name: War of the Confederation

zones.text: Arequipa, occupied by Chile from October 1837
Lima, occupied by Chile at the end of October 1838
the northern Argentine borderland occupied by Bolivia in 1838

wars.outcome: Chilean-Peruvian Restoration victory: the Confederate army was crushed at Yungay on 20 January 1839, Gamarra declared the Confederation dissolved on 25 August 1839 and the Chileans left on 19 October 1839; Peru was merged back into one state and Bolivia kept Tarija.
wars.note: Chile's Congress approved the declaration of war on 26 December 1836 (Confederation page). The two pages differ on Argentina: Rosas declared war on 19 May 1837 after Bolivia annexed Tarija (Confederation page) but on 9 May 1837 (War page). The Treaty of Paucarpata of 17 November 1837 was repudiated by Chile; the Bulnes expedition left Chile on 19 July 1838, the United Restoration Army won at Portada de Guías on 21 August 1838.

certainty.note: Neither page describes the Confederation's boundaries; the frontier in the Amazon, the Chaco and the Pacific coast of Bolivia (all in Cliopatria's shape) is approximate, and the Argentine border at Tarija was fought over.

notes: One Cliopatria shape (union of Bolivia's row and Peru's 1835 shape). Two pages of two. Not settled: (1) the page names North Peru and South Peru as separate member states with their own founding dates, but neither Cliopatria nor the project has rows for them; their capitals are not on the pages. (2) The Argentine front: the places Bolivia occupied in 1838 and the date of the return are not on either page (the occupation events are confidence 2 and 1); the Battle of Montenegro (24 June 1838) and Iruya are not on the pages opened. (3) The Chilean occupation events are recorded from the owner's side with the roles reversed (the schema says the owner records the same event); republic-of-chile has no events for 1837-1838, so the gap-filler for that dossier should add the Arequipa and Lima occupations and the war. (4) Peru's January 1839 restoration is the republic-of-peru dossier's date; the infobox end date is 25 August 1839, Bolivia's 26 October 1839, which is why identity.end is October 1839. (5) The shape includes the Acre, the Paraguayan Chaco and the Atacama coast of Cliopatria's Bolivia row, which no page opened here describes.
